key_insight: By restricting an unknown material coefficient to a low-dimensional latent family, the paper turns an ill-posed boundary inverse problem into a locally stable reconstruction task using only finitely many boundary excitations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to fast parameter identification in FEM-based mechanics and materials modeling, especially when repeated PDE solves are expensive.
method: Represent the coefficient with a C¹ latent parametrization, either analytic or learned from samples.
Use finitely many Dirichlet boundary excitations and the linearized Neumann-to-Dirichlet map to recover latent coordinates locally.
Accelerate the online inverse solve with neural surrogate forward models, with FEM refinement as an optional accuracy boost.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two-dimensional numerical experiments on inclusions and crack-like coefficients that demonstrate latent-space reconstruction, reduced online cost, and improved results with optional FEM refinement.
watch_item: The stability and error guarantees are local to a reference coefficient, so performance may degrade if the true material is far from the chosen latent neighborhood.
paper_title: Latent Inversion of Material Coefficients from Boundary Data via Finite Tests and Neural Surrogates
